tax_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST: CGST + SGST/UTGST, or IGST on inter-State supplies)
legal_ref: CGST Act 2017 s.9 and SGST Acts; IGST Act 2017 s.5; rate schedule Notification No. 9/2025-Central Tax (Rate) dated 17.09.2025 (w.e.f. 22.09.2025), superseding Notification No. 1/2017-Central Tax (Rate)
quote: "Rationalisation of the current 4-tiered tax rate structure into a citizen-friendly 'Simple Tax' - a 2 rate structure with a Standard Rate of 18% and a Merit Rate of 5%; a special de-merit rate of 40% for a select few goods and services"; "the changes in GST rates of goods and services need to be implemented with effect from 22 September 2025" — PIB release on 56th GST Council, 3 Sep 2025
source_title: PIB press release 'Recommendations of the 56th Meeting of the GST Council', 3 Sep 2025 (GST Council website)

reduced_rates.scope: merit rate from 22 Sep 2025: common household items, most food, drugs/medicines, agricultural and labour-intensive goods, hotel accommodation, etc.

special de-merit (higher) rate from 22 Sep 2025 for select luxury/sin goods and services; for pan masala, cigarettes, tobacco the old rate + compensation cess was retained until the cess account is discharged
nil-rated / exempt items (e.g. individual life and health insurance from 22 Sep 2025, UHT milk)

notes: Dual GST: intra-State supplies bear CGST + SGST/UTGST (18% = 9% + 9%), inter-State supplies and imports bear IGST at the combined rate. The Sept 2025 rationalisation (56th GST Council, effective 22 Sep 2025) removed the 12% and 28% slabs. Special low rates also exist (e.g. 3% gold/jewellery, 0.25% rough diamonds). Registration threshold generally INR 40 lakh (goods) / 20 lakh (services), lower in special-category States. GST Compensation Cess on tobacco/pan masala reportedly ended 1 Feb 2026, with those goods moved to 40% GST plus central excise / Health and National Security Cess.
